title: A PulseWidth-IN-PulseWidth-Out Universal Nonlinear Processing Element for Time-Domain In-Memory Computing Systems
problem: Time-domain in-memory computing lacks efficient nonlinear operators; frequent cross-domain data transmission (analog-to-digital-to-analog) degrades energy efficiency in edge AI systems.
motivation: Analog computing promises energy efficiency for edge AI, but nonlinear activations (ReLU, etc.) require repeated domain conversions that waste power and latency.
method: PIPO-UNPE: pulse-width IN/OUT universal nonlinear element implementing RRAM-based two-layer ReLU network in time domain; Dynamic Loss-Responsive Subset Enhancement (DLRSE) algorithm for improved function approximation; pulse-driven programmable current source; low-latency dispersion comparator VTC.
key_novelty: First time-domain universal nonlinear operator for analog in-memory computing avoiding cross-domain conversion overhead.
contributions: PIPO-UNPE: universal nonlinear processing element (ReLU network) in time domain
DLRSE algorithm improving function approximation of low-cost network
RRAM-based pulse-driven current source for efficient implementation
10 MNOPS at 912 uW; 9.5-25x energy efficiency gain in TD-IMC accelerator with <0.1% accuracy loss
limitations: Evaluation limited to ReLU networks; scalability to other nonlinear functions and deep networks not explored.
primary_theme: Time-domain universal nonlinear operator for integrated analog computing
